pass_condition: The identity hash is an include-list over the snapshot's own v2 rows: repositories + params + populations WHERE snapshot_id = ?.

findings.statement: The include-list keeps only `repositories`: the snapshot's params evidence rows and frozen populations are outside its identity hash and can be rewritten without detection.
findings.failure_scenario: On a snapshot with one repositories row, one params row and one populations row, rewriting the params row (score 88.0 -> 1.0, raw_value -> 999, source_hash -> deadbeef) leaves the identity hash unchanged ('snapA identity hash changed: False'), and so does forging the populations row (n -> 999, values_json -> [], values_hash -> forged). 03 section 5's served-database guard therefore certifies a database whose every 'why this score' row and every frozen ECDF population has been replaced.

observations: The scratch copy keeps exactly ['repositories'] -- verified directly in the same run.

params carries no snapshot_id column, so the fix is: after the repositories row filter, DELETE FROM params WHERE repo_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM repositories); DELETE FROM populations WHERE snapshot_id != ?; then keep those three tables.
The function name repositories_snapshot_dump_hash matches what it does today; on the fix it should become snapshot_dump_hash.
Mutant N2 proves the legacy exclusion is tested; nothing tests the params/populations inclusion because it does not exist.
